Inevitable

/in-EV-ih-tuh-bul/ — stress EV: 'in-EV-itable' · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Inevitable is certain to happen; impossible to avoid.

Once the ship's hull cracked, sinking became inevitable.

Worked Example

The old dam had cracked years ago, and every spring the crack widened. Engineers warned that no repair could hold, and that one day the water would break through no matter what anyone did.

The dam's failure was inevitable — certain to happen and impossible to avoid. A 'likely' event will probably occur; an inevitable one cannot be escaped at all.

How Inevitable Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

unavoidable

unavoidable: impossible to escape or prevent

certain

certain: sure to happen

inescapable

inescapable: impossible to get away from

Antonyms

avoidable

avoidable: able to be escaped or prevented

preventable

preventable: able to be stopped before it happens

How Strong Is It? — likely → inevitable → fated

likely vs. inevitable

likely vs. inevitable: Likely is weaker than inevitable — a likely event will probably happen, but an inevitable one cannot fail to happen.

fated vs. inevitable

fated vs. inevitable: Fated is stronger than inevitable — inevitable means nothing can stop it now, while fated suggests it was destined from the very beginning.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — in-

prefix — in-: not (Latin)

root — evit-

root — evit-: to avoid, shun (Latin)

suffix — -able

suffix — -able: able to be (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin evitare meant 'to avoid.' Add -able ('can be done') and in- ('not'), and inevitable literally means 'not able to be avoided.'

Use the root in a new word: invincible

Use the root in a new word: invincible: The chess champion seemed invincible until a teenager finally beat her.
